question: Can the context-enrichment mechanism even be instantiated on standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ), which use Freebase/Wikidata where triples lack source-passage provenance? If not, the idea's core mechanism is undefined for the strongest baselines and scope must narrow to text-grounded KGs.
description: The idea requires 'additional triples drawn from the same source passage'. Standard KGQA benchmarks use structured KGs without passages. Either (a) provenance-bearing text-grounded KGs must be adopted (e.g. HotpotQA supporting paragraphs, text-derived graphs), or (b) 'context' must be redefined as graph-neighborhood (k-hop around the target), which is very different and likely already explored.
confidence_basis: Based on reading the dataset descriptions of one benchmark paper (NSM) and abstracts of several KGQA papers; not an exhaustive survey of provenance-bearing KGs.
rationale: If provenance is unavailable, the proposed mechanism cannot be evaluated against the field's standard baselines and the contribution is at risk of being untestable as stated.
resolution: Partially resolved: the standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks are structured-KG benchmarks. NSM's full text states that WebQSP questions are 'answerable using Freebase as the knowledge base', and CWQ is generated from WebQSP, so neither carries source passages from which co-passage triples could be drawn; MetaQA is a synthetic movie KG. Therefore the mechanism cannot be evaluated on the standard benchmark suite without (a) switching to text-grounded KGs with provenance or (b) redefining context as graph neighbourhood, which is largely covered by subgraph retrieval work. A targeted search for provenance-bearing / text-derived KGs with co-passage triples is still needed.
